title: Vanishing descends through monic transitions from a scheme limit
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring, k:W→S a morphism of schemes, and G an etale Λ-module sheaf on W. Let D:I→Over W be a small cofiltered system with affine transitions and all structure maps to S quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Let c be a scheme limit cone, also quasi-compact and quasi-separated over S. Fix q∈Z and V over W. Suppose some D(i₀) maps to V and every transition from the higher image for V to one for D(i) induced by any map D(i)→V is monic. If the higher image for c.pt with the pulled-back G vanishes, then the higher image for V with the pulled-back G vanishes. Use [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions] for transitions and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] for higher images.

proof.text: Test the higher image for V on a geometric stalk. Map any element to the chosen stage i₀. Its image at the limit is zero by the vanishing hypothesis. Stalk continuity gives a later stage where this element is zero. Composition of canonical transitions identifies that map with the transition induced by the composite D(j)→D(i₀)→V. It is monic by hypothesis, so the initial stalk element was zero.
All geometric stalks are zero, so the map to the zero sheaf is an isomorphism by conservativity. Hence the original higher-image sheaf is zero.
